name: Waël Doulazmi

papers.title: Human-like autonomy emerges from self-play and a pinch of human data
papers.abstract: Self-play reinforcement learning has recently taken the wheel in autonomous driving. The approach uses cheap, large-scale simulation to substitute expensive, large-scale human driving data used by imitation learning approaches. While cost-effective, policies trained through self-play often behave unpredictably around humans; they fail to coordinate because they tend to converge to effective but incompatible driving conventions. Previous works attempt to mitigate such behavioral incompatibilities through reward engineering and domain randomization techniques, which are brittle and labor-intensive. We build on the best of both approaches and instead train driving policies using 30 minutes of human driving data and over 60 years of self-play simulation with a minimal reward function that solely encodes safe goal reaching. We call this _spiced self-play_: just as a pinch of a well-chosen ingredient can transform a dish, a small amount of human data, added as a behavioral anchor, disproportionately improves coordination with human drivers. Results show that our policies achieve improved coordination with real human driving trajectories using 2,500× less human data than imitation learning baselines. The entire pipeline completes in 15 hours on a single consumer-grade GPU. Together, our results point toward a positive revision of the field's understanding of data scaling: a small quantity of human data may suffice to regularize the vast space of driving policies toward ones that fit the road.
